candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients taking simvastatin to avoid grapefruit juice because it can increase simvastatin exposure and muscle-toxicity risk.

options.A: Grapefruit juice safely increases simvastatin's lipid-lowering effect without increasing toxicity
options.B: Grapefruit juice has no clinically relevant interaction with simvastatin
options.C: Avoid grapefruit juice because it can raise simvastatin levels and increase the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis
options.D: Drink grapefruit juice only when taking simvastatin with food to reduce muscle toxicity

candidate.rationale: The current simvastatin prescribing information states that grapefruit juice can raise plasma levels of simvastatin and may increase the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis; the intervention listed is to avoid grapefruit juice while taking simvastatin.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Grapefruit juice can raise simvastatin plasma levels, may increase risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis, and should be avoided.
candidate.source_locator: Drug Interactions, Section 7.1 > Grapefruit Juice > Clinical Impact and Intervention
candidate.source_version_date: Version 7 (current); label updated 2026-04-14; prescribing information revised 07/2025
candidate.stem: A client taking simvastatin asks whether grapefruit juice is safe to drink. Which response by the nurse is correct?
